main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}[Exact logarithmic-space derandomization] L=RL=BPL. \end{theorem}  \begin{theorem}[Acceptance-probability approximation] ... uniform deterministic algorithm which, on input (x,1^q) ... outputs an integer 0<=a<=2^{q+2} satisfying |a2^{-(q+2)}-p_M(x)|<=2^{-q}. It uses O(log(n+2)+q) work space and (n+2)^{O(1)}2^{O(q)} time.\end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: Every language decided by a polynomial-time, logarithmic-space randomized machine with two-sided bounded error is decidable deterministically in logarithmic space; more strongly, acceptance probabilities of such machines can be approximated to inverse-polynomial additive error in deterministic logspace and polynomial time, with no gap promise.

comparator.model: Machine q w h: finite control Fin(q+1), h read-only two-way input heads on Fin(n+2) with endmarkers (clamped moves), w binary work tapes indexed by Z (initially false), one fresh coin per step; output state halts. spaceThrough = sum over work tapes of #distinct head positions visited in steps 0..t; LogSpace: exists c>0, forall x, coins, t: spaceThrough <= c*clog2(n+2). L: Deterministic (transition ignores coin) & LogSpace & Decides. RL/BPL: LogSpace & HaltsBy c(n+2)^k on all coin tapes & acceptanceProbability (exact rational over Fin t -> Bool) >=1/2 / =0, resp. >=2/3 / <=1/3.

main_statement.match_check: Exact for Theorem 1.1 (class equality). Text diff: the 20 definition_names in the comparator are textually identical to OAI/Computability/Logspace/Deterministic.lean:1-130. Model is the standard one (multi-head two-way input is equivalent to single-head logspace; space counts visited work cells as in the paper's convention 'visiting a blank work cell counts toward space'). No loophole found: the time bound is on every coin tape, the space bound on every coin tape and every t.
main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: L=RL=BPL (and internally a fixed-precision estimator `fixed_precision_estimator`, Equality.lean:70, with error 1/32). NOT in the comparator: Theorem 1.2 (variable-precision approximation with explicit time/space), PromiseBPL=PromiseL, certified accepting computations, the effective compiler (lean/docs/103.md says so).

proof_architecture.claim: Configuration reduction: p(x)=((I-S)^{-1}e)(x0) for a strictly forward substochastic S with paired bounded-degree ports.

Correction-and-copy hierarchy: per stage, pilot detectors choose column multiplier g; k_* fixed iterations of the soft-threshold correction E (factorial truncation); residual D=C-E+EC; copies split remaining large entries; entries drop by 2^H while active vertices at most double; reward W_{l+1}=r(W_l+E_lW_l); after L=O(log n) stages W_L(primary copy) is within 1/16 (or 1/poly) of p.
Stochastic atoms: represent entries/corrections/detector scores by row-bounded sampled tables with exact conditional-mean identities in a shared O(log n)-bit environment of rank channels.
Conditional averaging: affine (SL_H(Z) x| Z^H) walks on retention slices with uniform spectral gap; validated variants let walks be described before endpoints are known.
Additive estimation: average budget differences with walks of length proportional to slack; mean errors telescope, noise contracts; dyadic slack groups.
